Posterior versus prior for heritabilities and genetic correlations

Source: R/plots.R
plot_prior_posterior.Rd

Posterior versus prior for heritabilities and genetic correlations

Usage

plot_prior_posterior(
  fit,
  trait_names = NULL,
  lkj_prior = NULL,
  n_prior = 4000,
  prior = NULL,
  ncol = 4
)

plot_forest(
  fit,
  trait_names = NULL,
  lkj_prior = NULL,
  n_prior = 4000,
  prior = NULL,
  prob = 0.95
)

Arguments

fit

A fit returned by lmm_animal, or a posterior draws object containing h2 and, for several traits, corrG.

trait_names

Optional trait names. Defaults to names recorded on the fit, or generic names when these are unavailable.

lkj_prior

Optional LKJ shape for the prior draws. The default NULL uses the shape recorded by the fit. Supplying a different shape warns that the comparison no longer uses the fitted prior. It is ignored, with a warning, for factor-G or univariate fits, or when prior is given.

n_prior

Passed to animal_prior_draws as n.

prior

Optional prior draws in the format returned by animal_prior_draws; computed if NULL and the fit's prior is known. Its parameter names and types must match the posterior. The caller is responsible for ensuring the draws represent the fitted prior.

ncol

Number of facet columns for plot_prior_posterior.

prob

Probability mass of the highest density interval, between 0 and 1.

Value

A ggplot object. plot_prior_posterior shows overlaid densities in one panel per parameter, and plot_forest shows means and prob intervals of the posterior and the prior.

Details

Where prior and posterior overlap, the data add little information.

The prior is drawn from the model configuration recorded by lmm_animal, so an "h2" fit is compared with its beta prior on the heritability and an unstructured fit with the LKJ shape it was given. A fit with correlation_prior = "size" or "shared_size" is compared with the size-factor prior on its genetic correlations (see animal_prior_draws); fits made before that argument existed are read as LKJ fits. For ordinary factor G, it simulates the regularized horseshoe loadings using the recorded factor count, global scale, slab and column decay, then constructs the genetic correlations. The current model uses the recorded beta prior on trait heritability; older factor fits recorded as "variance" use independent half-normal genetic and residual scales. These prior draws use R's random number generator.

The shared-factor model and a fit sampled from a custom model_file cannot be reconstructed here. Bare draws and older fits missing configuration metadata cannot establish which prior was used either. In each case pass prior with draws from the prior you used, using the same trait names as the posterior. The same rules apply to plot_forest().
